fundamental.thesis: Eris Lifesciences is a domestic branded-formulations company focused on chronic therapies such as diabetes and cardiac care, with almost no US-tariff exposure. Revenue growth has picked up from +7.4% YoY in Q1FY26 to +11.0% in Q3FY26 and +13.0% in Q1FY27 (₹873 cr). PAT rose +20.7% to ₹142 cr, a 16.3% PAT margin. However, EBITDA grew only +6.4% and EBITDA margin slipped from 35.9% to 34.2% YoY, so the PAT growth comes from below the operating line rather than from better operations. On the healthcare yardstick of P/E cross-checked against EV/EBITDA, the stock looks fair. Trailing P/E is 31.6x, inside the 28-40x pharma range. EV/EBITDA of 18.8x is below the broad-market median of 23.3x (P37), forward P/E of 23.1x implies expected earnings growth, and the stock sits at 34% of its 52-week range. The main risks are working-capital stress and estimates being cut. The current ratio fell to 0.60 from 0.93, collections and inventory turnover both slowed, debt/equity is 0.64, and consensus FY EPS has been cut 7.7% over 90 days while 9 of 10 analysts still rate it a buy. Q2FY27 results come on 26-Oct, so the latest data is one quarter old and a binary event is three days away.

fundamental.thesis: NATCO Pharma is a midcap generics maker whose earnings lean heavily on the US (tagged US revenue of Rs 3,760 cr against FY25 total revenue of Rs 4,430 cr), with a smaller domestic business that grew about 25% in Q3 FY26 and a clean FDA note for FY26. Revenue swung from +10.8% to -7.9% (Rs 4,078 cr) between FY25 and FY26 while PAT fell 24.8% to Rs 1,418 cr and PAT margin narrowed from 42.6% to 34.8%; Q1 FY27 figures were not extracted and the quarterly rows look non-comparable, but FY27 guidance of Rs 3,300-3,400 cr revenue and about Rs 750 cr PAT implies roughly -17% to -19% revenue and -47% PAT. Using earnings-based multiples with peak profits discounted, valuation is fair rather than cheap: trailing P/E of 11.2x is far below the 28-40x pharma range but sits on earnings expected to fall sharply, while forward P/E of 19.3x (about 21x on guided PAT) is a more modest discount, and conflicting price inputs (about Rs 798 from consensus versus about Rs 884 from the 52-week position) make these multiples approximate. The biggest risk is that the remaining business and planned acquisitions cannot replace the shrinking high-margin US profit, with results due on 13 Nov 2026 and the recent rights issue (17,058,082 shares) and promoter filings still to be assessed; the 7.74 debt/equity reading may be a percentage and needs checking.

The Ramco Cements is a mid-sized, South India-focused cement maker. The sector card describes the industry as consolidating, with UltraTech and Adani holding about 45% of capacity, which leaves smaller players like Ramco competing on price. Revenue growth has picked up, from -1.0% YoY in Q1FY26 to +9.6% in Q1FY27 and +10.0% in Q2FY27 (Rs 2,466 cr). Profit has gone the other way: Q2FY27 PAT fell 48.6% YoY to Rs 38 cr, a margin of just 1.6% versus 3.3% a year ago. EBITDA margin slid from 19.4% to 14.1% and EBITDA per tonne fell from Rs 981 to Rs 651 between Q1FY26 and Q3FY26, well below the Rs 900–1,100 band the sector card calls healthy. Q2FY27 profit also includes a Rs 4.8 cr exceptional gain and leaves out about Rs 8.6 cr of disputed mineral land tax, so underlying earnings are weaker than reported. I graded valuation on EV/EBITDA, the yardstick for capital-heavy cement; my verdict is expensive. At 17.1x EV/EBITDA, 30.1x trailing P/E (above the 12–22x Materials range) and 2.6x book for only a 9% ROE, the stock is priced for a margin recovery the filings don't yet show. Forward P/E of 28.7x is barely below trailing. The broad-market peer ranks (P31 on EV/EBITDA) compare it with unrelated sectors, so I gave them little weight. The stock trades near its 52-week low, but that alone is not a reason to buy.

fundamental.thesis: FSN E-Commerce (Nykaa) is India's leading online-plus-offline beauty platform with 65 million customers and 338 stores, plus a smaller Fashion arm that is still scaling. In Q2FY27 consolidated revenue grew 28% YoY to ₹3,006 cr and PAT rose 207% to ₹101 cr. Revenue growth has held steady at 27-29% for three quarters (+26.7%, +29%, +28%), and EBITDA margin has widened from 7.2% to 8.5% to 8.7%, against 6.8% a year ago. The key business metrics also look healthy: GMV is up 30%, Beauty EBITDA up 51% and House of Nykaa NSV up 36%, while Fashion's EBITDA margin is barely positive at 0.2%. For a platform business I judged valuation on EV/sales, EV/EBITDA and whether unit economics keep improving, not on trailing P/E. At about 8.5x sales and 106x EV/EBITDA (98th percentile of the market, forward P/E 112x at the 100th percentile), with the stock near the top of its 52-week range, the price already assumes years of margin gains, so I grade it expensive. The biggest risk is valuation, not execution: these names can drop 25-40% on a single growth or margin miss, and that risk is higher with no explicit FY27 guidance plus fresh spending on Nykaa NOW quick-commerce and the Simply Nam acquisition.

Zensar is an RPG-group mid-tier IT services firm with two businesses, Digital Services and Cloud Infrastructure, and it has a net cash position of ₹326 cr. Revenue is growing a little faster: H1FY27 revenue was ₹3,094 cr, up 10.2% YoY, compared with +7.5% to +8.7% through FY26, and Cloud Infrastructure grew 12.3%. Profit is not keeping up. H1 PAT of ₹374 cr rose only 2.7%, and PAT margin fell to 12.1% from 13.6% in FY26. Some of that drop is a one-off ₹24.9 cr Labour Code provision, but excluding it margin is still only about 12.9%. Cash conversion has also weakened, with CFO/PAT at 0.73x and only ₹22 cr of free cash flow because capex took up 8% of revenue, which is unusually high for an IT services firm. On valuation it looks cheap: trailing P/E is 12.6x against an IT sector band of 22–30x, EV/EBITDA is 8.2x (P7 across the market), and forward P/E of 11.2x is below trailing. Treat that discount with care, though. The stock is near its 52-week low, analysts have cut FY EPS estimates by about 1.2–1.4% over 90 days, and the market may be pricing in AI-driven shrinkage of mid-tier IT revenue. The feed also has several conflicting numbers: the Q1 revenue figure differs between sources, the Q2FY26 row is off by a factor of 10, and D/E of 1.68 and a 351% dividend yield contradict the net-cash position. So read the cheap grade with somewhat less confidence.

fundamental.thesis: Godfrey Phillips is a mid-cap cigarette-led business (Marlboro licensee, plus Four Square and Red & White) with smaller retail and confectionery arms, so it is a tobacco cash business rather than a typical FMCG name. The biggest risk is that the profit drop reflects lasting tax or volume pressure on cigarettes and keeps going.

fundamental.thesis: UPL is India's largest global agrochemical company, operating crop protection (UPL Corp), seeds (Advanta), and post-harvest segments across 130+ countries — a capital-intensive, leveraged cyclical recovering from a multi-year agrochem destocking cycle. Revenue has accelerated from a trough of +2% YoY in Q1FY26 to +10% YoY in Q1FY27 (₹10,181 cr consolidated); EBITDA grew 15% YoY to ₹1,500 cr with 180 bps contribution-margin expansion, and Q1FY27 PATMI was management's stated strongest in three years — a clear directional improvement from the -₹88 cr loss in Q1FY26, supported by broad-based platform growth (Advanta +26%, SUPERFORM +14%, UPL Corp +7%). Using EV/EBITDA as the primary yardstick for this capital-intensive business (per sector card guidance), UPL at 7.86× sits at P6 vs. 473 broad-market peers (67% discount to the 23.3× median) and at the mid-cycle floor for specialty chemicals (5–8× range); forward P/E of 12.65× is 46% below trailing 27.34×, signalling substantial earnings recovery priced in — the stock grades cheap on the appropriate metric. The primary risk is the combination of very high financial leverage (D/E flagged as extreme), NWC deteriorating sharply to 110 days (+24 days YoY from inventory build and FX translation), and persistent China-led price competition in agrochemicals — all amplified by rising crude input costs, INR weakness expanding USD-denominated debt service costs, and an ongoing RISK_OFF macro regime with FII net selling.

Brainbees (FirstCry) is India's largest multi-channel retailer for baby and kids products, with GlobalBees brand roll-ups, an international arm and preschools on the side. It is still not reliably profitable. In Q1FY27 consolidated revenue grew about 13% YoY, which management calls the best in 5 years, and India multi-channel grew 18% with same-store sales growth of 15%. Growth has been uneven rather than accelerating: +18.2% in FY25, then +11.4%, then +13.0%. Profitability is getting worse: adjusted EBITDA was flat YoY, India multi-channel EBITDA margin fell 290 bps, and the gross margin is still 260 bps short of where it was. The data for profit is unreliable: the trend table shows PAT of ₹51 cr (+34%), while yfinance shows a loss of ₹31 cr on revenue of ₹1,337 cr, and the filings index says its latest extracted results are from H1 FY26, so I am not relying on any PAT figure. The sector card says to judge loss-making platforms like this one on EV/sales, growth and unit economics, not P/E. On that basis the stock is fair rather than cheap: price/sales of 1.24x and P/B of 2.18x are low for a platform, but EV/EBITDA of 159x (most expensive in its peer set) and a forward P/E of 49x mean you are paying for a margin recovery that hasn't happened yet. The stock sits near its 52-week low, but analysts' FY estimates have been cut 15–18% over 90 days. The biggest risk is that Q2 results on 14 Nov show the promised gross-margin recovery not arriving, as quick-commerce and pharmacy competitors keep pressuring diapers (about 15% of GMV).

fundamental.thesis: HINDPETRO is a state-run oil marketing and refining company whose earnings depend mainly on the gap between crude costs and government-influenced retail fuel and LPG prices. Q2FY27 revenue was about ₹1,39,213 cr (H1 ₹2,84,339 cr minus Q1 ₹1,45,126 cr), up roughly 26% YoY from ₹1,10,323 cr, but this growth comes from higher prices rather than profit: Q2 PAT recovered to ₹3,625 cr (2.6% margin, partly helped by ₹3,960 cr of H1 LPG compensation) after a Q1 loss of ₹12,265 cr, leaving H1 at a ₹8,639 cr loss and H1 EBITDA margin at -1.9% versus about 6.7% a year earlier. Using P/E plus dividend yield and EV/EBITDA, the yardstick the sector card sets for OMCs, the headline 4.7x trailing P/E and 4.2x EV/EBITDA look like the cheapest in the market, but they are stale: they reflect FY26 PAT of ₹18,047 cr, while actual trailing-four-quarter PAT is only about ₹1,200 cr (roughly 70x). The 7.3x forward P/E is therefore better read as policy-priced and fair, not cheap. The biggest risk is crude above $100 with a weakening rupee: marketing losses could return while the balance sheet is already stretched, with short-term borrowings up to ₹35,933 cr, a current ratio of 0.57, negative interest coverage and an ₹18,049 cr unrecognised LPG under-recovery.

rules.eligible: growth == strong, risk != high, data_quality != poor, revenue growth not decelerating (newest results period's YoY revenue growth >= the preceding period's, from the filing extracts; a missing number passes)

rules.exit: growth -> weak, risk -> high, sentiment bearish with conviction >= 0.5, or the 120-session review failing (growth not strong, risk high or decelerating); between reviews never for decelerating, never for timing, never on missing data
